input.objective: Deploy MarginaliaPages v0.10 (src/MarginaliaPages.sol) on Ethereum mainnet: ONE contract, constructor (address hook, address annex, address intake, bytes32 action, address signer) = (0xf0457dd0cf526686190e4f057ba19db14d34a0cc the live MarginaliaHook of launch 1283, 0xd0c0d97aebe9194606bcc46ce56524eee4615543 the live MarginaliaAnnex of launch 1384, 0x1397434cd35e8a9C8aC312A61D3A285EB31dea56 the IdentityMD Intake, bytes32('oracle.request@oracle-1') the oracle action, 0x5598Aa9146215Bc13eb26f2c692Ad1461Fd32982 the IdentityMD oracle signer) — the same oracle constants the live hook holds as INTAKE, ACTION and ORACLE_SIGNER. This REPLACES the v0.9 Pages deployment of job 0925298b (old constants: 0.1 base, no cap, 90/5/5, no gate), which is not used. What it is: the page market of Marginalia, notes in the margin of every trade. A page of a writer's marginalia is the seat in that writer's room: the site delivers the writer's sealed notes and reasoning to page holders first. Pages are bought and sold against a CAPPED linear bonding curve priced in IMD 0xD34a99Bc0f67aE1bbd63C660e6d0b0dd03E263B7: page n costs min(BASE 0.05 IMD x n, CAP 10 IMD), so the line meets the cap at page CAP_PAGE 200 and every later page costs 10 IMD (priceOf sums the line segment and the flat tail; the curve reserve always covers every holder selling out at any depth). Pages are never transferable (buy and sell on the curve only) and a wallet holds at most MAX_PER_WALLET 10 pages of one subject (TooManyPages). BUY GATE (sell is never gated): eligible(wallet) is true when the wallet holds at least MARG_GATE 10,000 MARG (hook.token(), 0xfa0efea559bde229031c2b0a219472316647759c), OR has posted at least one note on the hook or the annex (the first two words of either contract's records(address) getter: score, posted), OR is on identity.md's settled WhitelistCurator at the fixed address WHITELIST 0xcB0b0531e86A9aC36Fa865cA8e3dbccF047FDA91 (contributedBy(address) > 0, read by staticcall, a failed read counts as not listed); otherwise buy reverts NotEligible. Every trade pays FEE_BPS = 10% of its value: ISSUER_BPS 80% of the fee to the issuer in IMD, BURN_BPS 10% of the fee buys MARG on the launch pool through the hook's PoolManager (a quiet buy, no hook fee; unlockCallback accepts only the PoolManager) and sends it to 0x000000000000000000000000000000000000dEaD, the remaining 10% of the fee goes to the hook's pools through hook.fundPot. An issuer is any address (subjectOf(address) pays itself) or an X handle nobody has claimed (subjectOfHandle(string), lower-cased and validated on chain: 1-15 of a-z 0-9 underscore): pages of a handle trade on the same curve while the issuer's 80% waits in escrow. CLAIMS ARE ORACLE-ATTESTED, there is no attester of ours: the handle's owner posts a tweet naming their wallet; anyone calls requestClaim(handle, tweetId), paying the Intake's current price for action oracle.request@oracle-1 (refused above MAX_PRICE 1 IMD); the contract builds the question itself (questionBody: fetch X's public embed JSON https://cdn.syndication.twimg.com/tweet-result?id=<tweetId>&token=a, if user.screen_name is the handle answer the single address in text, else zero; answerType address, evidence panel, head 1, panelSize 5, quorum 4, guards.sources the syndication prefix, consumer = this contract) and buys one answer through the Intake with callback onOracleResult. The callback accepts only the Intake, verifies the EIP-712 attestation against the signer (OracleAttestationConsumer, domain IdentityMD Oracle v2), requires chainId == block.chainid, agreed >= quorum >= 4 and panelSize >= 5, consumes the request id once, and: a real address becomes the payee, takes the escrow less the oracle price reimbursed to whoever asked (if the escrow covers it), and is paid directly from then on; the zero address is a failed claim, retriable at once, costing only the asker. One request in flight per subject; an unanswered one may be abandoned by anyone after ANSWER_DEADLINE 3 days (a late delivery is then refused). One successful claim per subject ever. Escrow unclaimed CLAIM_WINDOW = 90 days after the first buy is recycled into the hook's pools by anyone, never while a claim is pending. No owner, no pause, no upgrade, no attester, nonReentrant trades, claims and callback. The constructor reads no chain state (the launcher rehearses constructors in an empty EVM); it stores the five values (annex may be zero: that gate leg is then off). Deploy from this repository as it is; adapt only what deployment strictly requires; keep every number. Tests: forge test --match-path test/Pages.t.sol (14 tests against the local hook, a whitelist mock etched at the fixed address, an annex-records mock, a local Intake mock and an EOA signer, incl. the capped curve at 210 pages, the per-wallet limit, every gate leg and ungated selling, the 200k callback stipend and replay/tamper refusals).

_check.note: PAGES v0.10 (operator decisions 2026-10-12): capped curve 0.05 x n to 10 IMD at page 200, 10 pages per wallet, buy gate (whitelist OR 10,000 MARG OR a posted note), 80/10/10 split. SEQUENCE: the Annex launches first; annex address filled 2026-10-12 (launch 1384, 0xd0c0d97a…); push the snapshot as release/pages-v2 (never force main), re-check, then the operator pays 0.5 IMD. The v0.9 job 0925298b deploys an unused contract.
